title: Privacy documentation experiment
subtitle: Open-source AI/ML projects with an expanded discovery vocabulary
heroNote: This page brings together the sample, retrieved documents, textual evidence, methodology, statistical results, and reproduction instructions. Displayed values are generated directly from versioned repository artifacts.
sampleFilesText: The file used by the pipeline is available at selected_repositories.csv. The configured vocabulary is available at ai_ml_topics_used.csv.
inspectionIntro: Detailed records are not repeated on this page. The complete list of repositories, documents, classifications, evidence, and metadata remains available in the versioned files below:
dataLinksList:
• Complete final dataset
  • Sample used
  • Positive evidence
  • Raw JSONL checkpoint
  • Run manifest
designText: The study compares the same set of repositories in two historical snapshots: the last commit up to May 24, 2018, and the last commit up to June 30, 2026. The unit of analysis is a public AI/ML repository.
selectionAfter: Rscript main.R --select creates a fresh sample and collects the historical snapshots. Then Rscript main.R --analyze validates the collection, reruns the offline analysis, and generates the site. Rscript main.R --run executes the entire flow from start to finish.
documentationIntro: Root READMEs and textual documents whose names or paths indicate privacy, security, data protection, terms, consent, retention, or compliance are analyzed. D1 indicates contextualized documentary evidence. The PDE Score sums seven criteria:
criteriaList:
1. personal data;
  2. processing purpose;
  3. legal basis;
  4. data-subject rights;
  5. retention or deletion;
  6. sharing or transfer;
  7. protection against leakage or unauthorized access.
documentationNegative: Isolated mentions, bibliographies, tests, examples, dependencies, and link lists are not sufficient to mark a criterion.
statisticsText: For D1, the pipeline computes the exact two-sided McNemar test. For the PDE Score, it computes the exact paired Wilcoxon test, excluding zero differences and using average ranks for ties. The significance level is α=0.05.
partitionText: Queries are partitioned by creation date when the estimated count approaches the Search API limit of 1,000 results. Downloaded partitions and pages are recorded in the selection manifest.
resultLimitations: The results measure versioned documentary evidence. They are not a legal audit and do not support attributing causality exclusively to GDPR.
requirementsList:
• R 4.5 or later;
  • the jsonlite package for the pipeline;
  • knitr, rmarkdown, and Quarto to render this site;
  • yaml to read settings.yml;
  • curl for new GitHub API calls;
  • a GITHUB_TOKEN only when a new collection is required.

statusText: main.R shows progress by stage and writes its state to outputs/metadata/run_status.json. During selection, it reports the topic, pages downloaded, and total results; during collection, it reports complete and incomplete pairs and an estimated remaining time. The normal API interval does not produce repeated messages; actual GitHub limits are shown with an estimated retry time.

templates.main-result: Before GDPR, {preD1} of {pairs} repositories showed documentary evidence of privacy (D1=1). In the post-GDPR period, the count was {postD1} repositories. The exact two-sided McNemar test resulted in {mcnemar}.
templates.score-result: The mean PDE Score increased from {preScore} to {postScore}. The exact paired Wilcoxon test resulted in {wilcoxon}.
templates.vocabulary-coverage: Discovery was expanded from three base topics to {topics} topics while preserving eligibility criteria and documentary analysis. The expansion includes established subdomains and recent AI/ML terms; a topic remains a discovery signal, not automatic proof of technical scope.
templates.sample-description: The sample contains {repositories} repositories with an SPDX-identified license approved by OSI.
templates.selection-description: The selector queries {topics} topics configured in settings.yml, covering base topics, subdomains such as computer vision, natural language processing, and object detection, plus extensions such as LLMs, transformers, generative AI, diffusion, multimodality, RAG, and agents. It then applies the same criteria for public visibility, an SPDX/OSI-approved license, non-fork and non-archived status, creation before May 25, 2018, at least 500 stars, at least 100 real issues, at least 24 months of activity, and activity before and after the reference date.
templates.selection-manifest-available: The manifest for this run is available in the artifacts.
templates.selection-manifest-pending: The manifest will be produced when the expanded selection is run with a GitHub token.
templates.pvalue-explanation: The p-value is the probability of observing a result at least as extreme as the one obtained, assuming that the null hypothesis (H0) is true. With α=0.05, a p-value below α leads to rejection of H0; a value greater than or equal to α does not support rejecting it. This decision does not prove H1 or turn H0 into an automatic truth.
templates.pvalue-result: In this study, the exact McNemar p-value was {mcnemar} and the Wilcoxon value was {wilcoxon}. The statistical decision should be updated together with the counts whenever a new sample is generated and should consider effect size and the limitations of the observational design.
